procedures.title: Check the engine oil level
steps: Park on level ground. Warm up the engine, turn it off, and wait for the oil to drain back (about 5 minutes per P.529; P.621 says about 8).
Holding a rag under the end, pull the dipstick out and wipe it clean.
Reinsert the dipstick fully.
Pull it out again and check the oil level is above the low level mark.
Wipe the dipstick and reinsert it fully.
warnings: Check the level regularly to prevent serious engine damage.
If the level is above the upper limit mark, contact a Toyota dealer.
procedures.notes: Oil use rises in a new engine, with heavy loads or towing, frequent acceleration/deceleration, and long idling. Level can rise from fuel/moisture if the engine is often not fully warmed up (short trips, low speeds, cold weather).

procedures.title: Add engine oil
steps: Remove the oil filler cap by turning it counterclockwise.
Add engine oil of the same type slowly, checking the dipstick.
Keep the level between the low level mark and the refill upper limit mark (1.5 qt / 1.4 L apart).
Install the oil filler cap by turning it clockwise.
warnings: Avoid overfilling, which can damage the engine.
Dispose of used oil and filters properly; do not put them in household trash, sewers, or on the ground.

procedures.title: Reset the oil maintenance data after an oil change
steps: Use the meter control switch to open the multi-information display settings.
Select 'Vehicle Settings' (press and hold the enter button).
Select 'Oil Maintenance', then choose 'Yes'.
Wait for the confirmation message on the multi-information display.
procedures.notes: The truck tracks oil maintenance itself. The button sequence differs slightly between the 7-inch and 12.3-inch displays (P.530-531).

procedures.title: Reset the 'maintenance required' message
steps: Use the meter control switch to open the multi-information display settings.
Select 'Vehicle Settings' (press and hold the enter button).
Select 'Scheduled Maintenance', then choose 'Yes'.
procedures.notes: Do this after the required maintenance is performed according to the schedule. Button sequence differs between the 7-inch and 12.3-inch displays.

procedures.title: Check the engine coolant
steps: With the engine cold, check that the level in the reservoir is between the 'F' and 'L' lines.
If it is at or below the 'L' line, add coolant up to the 'F' line.
If the level drops again soon after topping up, check the radiator, hoses, reservoir cap, drain cock and water pump for leaks, or have the dealer test it.
warnings: Never remove the coolant reservoir cap when the engine is hot; the system is pressurized and can spray hot coolant.

procedures.title: Check the radiator, condenser, and intercooler
steps: Look for foreign objects on the radiator, condenser and intercooler and clear them away.
If any is extremely dirty or you are unsure of its condition, have the dealer inspect it.
warnings: Do not touch the radiator or intercooler when hot.

procedures.title: Check and add brake fluid
steps: Check that the fluid level is between the 'MAX' and 'MIN' lines on the reservoir.
If adding, use only the specified brake fluid type (see the brake fluid spec) from a newly opened container, with a clean funnel.
warnings: Brake fluid absorbs moisture, which can cause a dangerous loss of braking efficiency.
Brake fluid can harm skin, eyes and paint; flush skin/eyes with clean water immediately.
A slow small drop is normal as pads wear; frequent refilling can mean a serious problem.

procedures.title: Check the battery
steps: Check that the terminals are not corroded and there are no loose connections, cracks, or loose clamps.
Check the terminals, hold-down clamp and bracket.
warnings: When recharging with the battery installed, disconnect the ground cable and keep the charger switched off while connecting/disconnecting.
Recharging produces flammable, explosive hydrogen gas.
procedures.notes: After recharging or reconnecting the battery the engine may not start. Follow the initialization steps on P.534 (automatic: shift to P; open and close a door; restart).

procedures.title: Check the tires
steps: Check whether the treadwear indicators (TWI marks) are showing.
Check for uneven wear, such as excessive wear on one side of the tread.
Check the spare tire's condition and pressure if it has not been rotated in.
Check inflation pressure when the tires are cold against the value for your tire type.

procedures.title: Rotate the tires
steps: Rotate the tires in the order shown in the manual's diagram (P.538), on the maintenance schedule.
procedures.notes: The rotation pattern is a diagram in the manual, not text. The interval comes from the Scheduled Maintenance Guide.

procedures.title: Replace the air conditioning (cabin) filter
steps: Remove the filter cover (release the claws), then the filter case.
Take the old filter out of the case and put in a new one.
Make sure the 'UP' marks on the filter and the case point up.
procedures.notes: Inspect and replace per the maintenance schedule; replace early in dusty areas or heavy traffic. Some early steps were not captured in the text extraction (P.553).

procedures.title: Replace the electronic key battery
steps: Take out the mechanical key.
Remove the cover (tape the screwdriver tip to avoid damaging the key).
Remove the depleted battery and insert a new CR2450 with the '+' terminal facing up.
warnings: The key can be damaged if this is done incorrectly; Toyota recommends the dealer do it.

procedures.title: Check and replace fuses
steps: Turn the engine switch off and open the fuse box cover.
Remove the suspect fuse (only type A can use the pullout tool).
Check whether it is blown.
Replace a blown type A or B fuse with one of the same amperage (printed on the fuse box lid). For type C and D, contact the dealer.
warnings: Never use a higher amperage fuse, a wire, or any other object in place of a fuse.
If a replaced fuse blows again, have the dealer inspect the vehicle.
procedures.notes: Fuse boxes: engine compartment (types A and B), passenger-side instrument panel, and under the right-hand rear seat on vehicles with rear seats.

procedures.title: Replace the front turn signal/parking light bulb (bulb type)
steps: Remove the 4 push clips and the air cleaner inlet (passenger's side only).
Turn the bulb base counterclockwise and remove the bulb.
Install the new bulb and turn the base clockwise.
Reinstall the air cleaner inlet and push clips (passenger's side only).
warnings: Do not replace a bulb right after the lights have been on; bulbs get very hot.
Do not touch the bulb glass with bare hands.
Make sure the bulb is fully seated and locked.

schedule_sources.title: Toyota Tacoma Maintenance Schedule

general_rule.quote: Typically, it means scheduling service every six months or every 5,000 miles, whichever comes first.

caveats: A dealership marketing page, not Toyota's official guide. Provided by the user as the schedule to log.
States no model year, and says 'specific tasks may vary based on your Tacoma's model, year, and driving conditions.' Applicability to the 2026 Tacoma is unconfirmed.
The page says service intervals occur at 5,000, 15,000 and 30,000 miles, but then lists tasks at other mileages too.
It never states an oil interval in words. Oil changes appear at 10,000, 20,000, 30,000 ('Change engine air filter and oil'), 40,000 and 50,000 ('Additional oil change').
Cabin air filter wording is inconsistent: inspect at 10,000/15,000/45,000, replace at 20,000, 40,000 and 50,000, and 25,000 explicitly excludes replacement.
No time-based oil interval (months) and no severe-conditions schedule is given.
Milestone text is logged as written. Some entries, such as 'Repeat all standard 5,000-mile maintenance', refer back to the 5,000-mile list.
